paper_000.title: Population-based heteropolymer design to mimic protein mixtures
key_findings: 2D informative sequence analysis parameterizes chemical characteristics and sequential arrangement at segmental level
Random heteropolymers (RHPs) can mimic protein conformational diversity
PCA overlap between RHP ensembles and proteins governs interplay
Segmental similarity determines ability to replicate protein functions
paper_000.relevance_to_task: Provides framework for statistically replicating protein sequence features in synthetic heteropolymers

paper_001.title: Practical Prediction of Heteropolymer Composition and Drift
key_findings: Mayo-Lewis model predicts copolymer composition and drift
Monte Carlo simulation enables user-friendly prediction
Reactivity ratios determine monomer distribution along chains
paper_001.relevance_to_task: Supports the statistical design approach for hydrogel monomer compositions

paper_002.title: Mussel-Inspired Adhesives and Coatings
key_findings: Mussel byssal plaques achieve ~6 MPa adhesive strength underwater
Dopa (catecholic functionality) is key to wet adhesion
Water undermines adhesion through dielectric screening
Successful wet adhesives must displace water at interface
paper_002.relevance_to_task: Establishes biological benchmark (6 MPa) and design principles for underwater adhesion

design_principles_extracted: Hydrophobic content positively correlates with adhesive strength (r=0.65)
Amide content negatively correlates with adhesive strength (r=-0.59)
High performers show elevated Hydrophobic-BA (~63%) and reduced Amide-AAm (~0.8%)
Target >1 MPa requires optimization beyond current maximum (~321 kPa achieved)
